headline: High-risk shared filesystem and MCP pathways create prompt-injection, data-leakage, and write-conflict exposure between Gemini CLI and Semantic Kernel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can read/write repo files and use MCP; Semantic Kernel can also use MCP and read/write application-defined files. That creates a plausible content-to-instructions bridge if either agent consumes the other's files or MCP outputs as trusted input. The pair is not provably isolated, so this is more than manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF agent_a reads files produced by agent_b as instructions
IF agent_b ingests agent_a-generated file content or MCP output without provenance checks
mitigations: Disable shared MCP servers for the pair
Separate workspaces so each agent sees only its own files
Add a provenance header check before parsing any cross-agent file
Require manual review of any agent-generated instructions
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read filesystem content and send data to external model APIs. Gemini CLI touches source code, cwd files, and shell environment; Semantic Kernel touches application context and can call Azure/OpenAI/Hugging Face/MCP tools. In a shared workspace, sensitive files can flow from one agent into the other's outbound API calls.
conditions: IF agent_a and agent_b share a workspace containing secrets or sensitive source
IF either agent forwards read file contents into its model backend or plugins
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Remove secrets from the shared workspace before running
Restrict outbound API keys to least-privilege test accounts
Turn off automatic file ingestion where possible
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any API call

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI has unrestricted filesystem write and modify_git_state, while Semantic Kernel also has filesystem write and broad API/plugin access. The profiles show shared-state via filesystem/git for agent_a and application-defined files for agent_b, so concurrent writes can collide and corrupt repo or state. No locking mechanism is documented, so uncertainty pushes this to high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory or git branch
IF agent_b plugins mutate files while agent_a is editing the repo
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch
Use separate working directories
Pause one agent before the other writes
Require explicit lock files for shared resources
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level write serialization

D_cascading_error.rationale: Semantic Kernel is an orchestration layer that can treat upstream agent output as plugin or agent input, and Gemini CLI can generate code, shell commands, and file edits. If SK consumes Gemini output without verification, errors can cascade into downstream actions or persisted artifacts. The pair is not documented as having a verification boundary, so the interaction is risky by default.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output as authoritative input
IF agent_b executes or persists agent_a-generated commands, code, or facts without review
mitigations: Insert a human review step before execution
Require schema validation on agent_a outputs
Limit agent_a to draft-only mode
Log and diff all downstream actions
requires-engineering: add automated verification against source data

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are docs-only open-source tools with broad network/API access and secret handling, but no residency or retention guarantees are documented. Because agent_b can route through Azure/OpenAI/Hugging Face and agent_a through Google APIs, compliance risk arises if regulated data is processed under mismatched provider policies. The missing policy detail forces a conservative medium rating.
conditions: IF regulated data is sent through either agent's external API calls
IF the deployment requires residency or retention guarantees not provided by the configured providers
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in prompts and files
Use provider accounts with approved compliance settings
Document retention and residency for each API
Restrict secrets to test-only credentials
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement and audit logging
